title: Complete Noetherian local rings are excellent
statement: Every commutative Noetherian local ring $A$ that is complete for its maximal-ideal-adic topology is excellent [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], [def-exc-excellent-ring].

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak m$ be the maximal ideal of $A$. The assumed completeness is maximal-ideal-adic completeness, including separatedness. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-g-ring] to $(A,\mathfrak m)$: its hypotheses are precisely Noetherianity, locality, and this completeness. Thus $A$ is a G-ring.

source.place: Tag 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent, first sentence; Tag 07PX, proposition-ubiquity-G-ring, case (2), using Tag 07PS, proposition-Noetherian-complete-G-ring.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary commutative $A$-algebra $B$ finite as an $A$-module. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product], $B$ is Noetherian. For any prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$, put $D=B/\mathfrak q$. This is a domain: a product of residue classes is zero only if one factor is zero, by primality, and $1$ is nonzero because $\mathfrak q$ is proper. If $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ generate $B$ as an $A$-module, their classes generate $D$, since reducing $b=\sum_i a_ib_i$ modulo $\mathfrak q$ gives the required expression for every class. Hence $D$ is a finite $A$-algebra. The domain clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product] now makes $D$ a Noetherian complete local domain. Apply [lem-per-complete-local-domain-regular-open] to obtain a nonempty open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}D$ on which every local ring is regular. This holds for every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$.

source.place: Tag 07PJ, proposition-ubiquity-J-2, proof of case (2); Tag 07PI, lemma-complete-Noetherian-domain-J-0; finite-algebra completeness is Algebra Tag 0325, lemma-quotient-complete-local.

proof.text: The arbitrary finite algebra $B$ in Step 2 is Noetherian, and every prime quotient $B/\mathfrak q$ has a nonempty regular open. These are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-exc-regular-locus-open-from-prime-quotients]. It follows that the regular locus of $B$ itself is open. Since $B$ was arbitrary, every finite $A$-algebra has open regular locus, including the zero algebra, whose spectrum and regular locus are empty.

source.place: Tag 07PJ, proposition-ubiquity-J-2, proof of case (2), applying Tag 07P9, lemma-intersection-regular-with-closed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-j2-finite-algebra-criterion] to the Noetherian ring $A$ and the conclusion of Step 3. Every finite type $A$-algebra has open regular locus. Thus $A$ satisfies the J-2 condition; this argument has not assumed that $A$ itself is reduced or a domain.

source.place: Tag 07PJ, proposition-ubiquity-J-2, proof of case (2), using condition (3) of Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2.

proof.text: Noetherianity means every ideal is finitely generated, so $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated. The Cohen structure theorem [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-structure-power-series-surjection] therefore supplies $n\geq0$, a coefficient ring $\Lambda$ which is either a field or a Cohen ring, and a surjection $\pi:S=\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\twoheadrightarrow A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], $S$ is a Noetherian regular local ring. This includes $n=0$ and both residue-characteristic cases.

source.place: Tag 032C, remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary, first three sentences, using Tag 032A, theorem-cohen-structure-theorem.

proof.text: For every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $S$, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] gives regularity of $S_{\mathfrak p}$. Together with the Noetherianity of $S$ from Step 5, this is exactly the hypothesis of [lem-trf-regular-ring-universally-catenary]. Hence $S$ is universally catenary.

source.place: Tag 032C, remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary, final sentence; Tags 00NQ, lemma-regular-ring-CM, and 00NM, lemma-CM-ring-catenary; regular-local localization is Tag 0AFS.

proof.text: Let $T$ be any finite type $A$-algebra, generated by $t_1,\ldots,t_r$. It is also finite type over $S$: express any $t\in T$ as a polynomial in the $t_i$ with coefficients in $A$ and lift each of the finitely many coefficients along the surjection $\pi:S\twoheadrightarrow A$. The resulting polynomial expression with coefficients in $S$ has the same value in $T$. Universal catenarity of $S$ now says that $T$ is catenary, with the finite bound on prime-chain lengths and the equality of saturated-chain lengths in [def-exc-excellent-ring]. These are properties of the ring $T$, independent of which coefficient ring was used. As $T$ was arbitrary, the Noetherian ring $A$ is universally catenary. This is the quotient-descent argument, written directly from the finite-type and universal-catenarity definitions.

source.place: Tag 032C, remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary, quotient consequence; universal catenarity is Tag 00NL, definition-universally-catenary.

proof.text: Finally $A$ is Noetherian by hypothesis, a G-ring by Step 1, and J-2 by Step 4, so it is quasi-excellent by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Step 7 gives universal catenarity. The same definition therefore makes $A$ excellent.

source.place: Tag 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent, clause (2), and Tag 07QT, definition-excellent.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent, clause (2) and its proof; J-2 follows the proof of Tag 07PJ case (2), and universal catenarity follows Algebra Tag 032C.
